jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Oklahoma, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Oklahoma, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, Oklahoma Senate, Oklahoma House and U.S. House districts, cities and towns, school districts and ZIP codes.
jsonld.keywords: Oklahoma district map, what district am I in, Oklahoma Senate district, Oklahoma House district, Oklahoma congressional district, Oklahoma school district lookup

brand.tagline: Every civic district that covers your point in Oklahoma, and who represents you there.

head.title: Oklahoma district lookup — districtry Oklahoma
head.description: Tap the map or search an Oklahoma address: county, Oklahoma Senate, Oklahoma House and U.S. House districts — and who represents you.
head.og_description: Every civic district that covers a point in Oklahoma, and who holds it.
head.og_image_alt: districtry Oklahoma — every district that covers a point, and who represents it.
head.twitter_description: Click or search an Oklahoma address to see every district that covers it.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 5 congressional districts — the largest districts Oklahoma carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 5 features for Oklahoma, measured 2026-10-09. The layer's own district field is CD120.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Oklahoma Senate District
layers.rank_note: 48 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Oklahoma Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 48 features, measured 2026-10-09. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 20 m interval and refused over a 25 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ok-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Open States current-people export for Oklahoma (name, party, e-mail, the member's own page). The export carries no capitol office or telephone for any member; reading those from the Senate's own site is recorded in ok/WATCH.md.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 77 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 77 features, measured 2026-10-09.

source.people: ok-county-commissioners.json, from the Oklahoma State Election Board's Roster of State and County Officers (the 2024 edition, compiled after the November 5, 2024 general election), rebuilt weekly by CI. The card lists the county's three commissioners and the county's information telephone line. The roster is a snapshot the counties do not keep current between elections, and the card says so.

layers.label: Conservation District
layers.rank_note: The 84 conservation districts on the Oklahoma Conservation Commission's map, pre-built with the app — 2,155 km2 mean area (median 1,931, smallest 779, largest 5,967), measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a county (2,351) and larger than a House district (1,792). 77 of the 84 lie within one county; they cover the state bar 67 km2 of slivers.

source.answers: The conservation district covering the point — the primary local unit of government Oklahoma law makes responsible for conserving the state's renewable natural resources — and the district's office.

boundary.label: Oklahoma Conservation Commission — cons_dis, layer 0 on ArcGIS Online: 84 districts in 106 records, measured 2026-10-16, pre-built by ok/scripts/build_ok_conservation_districts.py and shipped with the app. The layer states no licence.

source.people: Four districts' five directors, from each district's own website (Tulsa County, Dewey, Rogers and Deer Creek), read by ok/scripts/build_ok_conservation_directors.py and dated on the card. The Commission's directory of district offices, read by ok/scripts/build_ok_conservation_offices.py, gives each district's office, telephone and e-mail, and the card shows them, credited to the Commission, whose website terms of use allow personal, non-commercial use of its content. The directory names none of a district's five directors, so for the other 80 districts the card names no one and says how the board is chosen.
source.applies: Oklahoma — statewide; the 84 districts cover the state bar 67 km2 of slivers, most of them along the Kansas line in Texas County.

layers.label: Oklahoma House District
layers.rank_note: 101 House districts — the smallest of the three chamber tilings

source.answers: The Oklahoma House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 101 features, measured 2026-10-09.

source.people: ok-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Open States current-people export for Oklahoma.

layers.label: Judicial District
layers.rank_note: 26 judicial districts of whole counties, 6,963 km2 mean area, measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file — larger on average than a State Senate district (3,771 km2), smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The judicial district covering the point, its district judge offices and the counties whose voters elect each one.

boundary.label: Dissolved from the shipped county fabric (TIGERweb State_County layer 1) by ok/scripts/build_ok_judicial_districts.py, following the Oklahoma State Election Board's 2024 Roster of State and County Officers (published March 2025): its district judge offices with the counties that elect each, checked against the same roster's key to districts by county. The statutes were not read: both of the state's publishers of them refuse this project in robots.txt.

source.people: No judge is named yet; recorded as gap ok-judicial-district-judges. The roster names each judge beside their home town, which this project never copies. The card links the roster.

layers.label: School District (Unified)
layers.rank_note: 415 unified districts, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive; with the 91 elementary districts they cover the state exactly

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 415 features for Oklahoma, measured 2026-10-09.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. Oklahoma's school boards are elected, and no statewide roster of their members was established in this pass — recorded as gap ok-school-board-members.
source.applies: Oklahoma — every point outside the 91 elementary districts. The two tilings partition the state: their Census land areas sum to exactly the 77-county total, measured 2026-10-09. TIGERweb's secondary tiling is empty for Oklahoma (0 features).

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 666 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas overlapping Oklahoma, of the 1,058 in the state's own bounding box, in a mirrored tile archive (measured 2026-10-17); the layer hides outside Oklahoma

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='40'. 1,058 features in Oklahoma's box, measured 2026-10-09.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Oklahoma. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code (Wichita Falls TX gives 76301).

layers.label: School District (Elementary)
layers.rank_note: 91 elementary (dependent) districts, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive; the ground the unified tiling leaves

source.answers: The elementary school district covering the point, where the point is in one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 2 (elementary school districts), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 91 features for Oklahoma, measured 2026-10-09.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. Oklahoma's school boards are elected, and no statewide roster of their members was established in this pass — recorded as gap ok-school-board-members.
source.applies: Oklahoma — the 91 elementary districts, 11,441 km2 of land between them. Everywhere else the unified card is the answer.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 600 incorporated cities and towns, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The city or town containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 600 features for Oklahoma (165 cities, 435 towns), measured 2026-10-09.

source.people: In the 16 cities above 25,000 people, the mayor and every council member or commissioner, written down from each city's own pages and proved against those pages by ok/scripts/build_ok_city_councils.py, which fails when a name is no longer on the page it cites (ok/data/app/ok-city-councils.json). Where the page a seat cites prints an e-mail address or a telephone number beside that member alone, the card shows it, and the build proves it on that page in the same way; a line or mailbox the page gives the office or several members is not shown, and no street address is. Muskogee's website does not let this app read it, so its names come from the county election board's official results for February 10, 2026 and from news reports, and the card says so. Each seat says whether its ward's own voters or the whole city elect it, read from each city's charter, its own pages, a county election board's results or news reports, because nothing the state publishes records it. Oklahoma's other cities and towns name nobody yet, recorded as gap ok-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: Oklahoma — statewide. A point outside every city and town is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: City Council District
layers.rank_note: 64 council wards and districts in the 10 cities above 25,000 people whose wards elect their own members and are drawn, ranked just after City or Town, which each one divides, so a ward draws on top of its city

source.answers: The city council ward or district containing the point, in the 10 Oklahoma cities above 25,000 people whose wards elect their own members and are drawn, and the member or members for it.

boundary.label: City of Oklahoma City — Council Wards, layer 2 of its Government_Boundaries service, served through ArcGIS Online: 8 wards, read 2026-10-16, the ward number alone requested. It states no licence.

City of Tulsa — Council Districts, in the city's ArcGIS Online organization, carrying the metes-and-bounds description of each election district and last edited 29 January 2026: 9 districts, read 2026-10-16, the district number alone requested. Its credit lines name INCOG and the City of Tulsa GIS Department, it says it "should only be used as a supplement to official records", and it states no licence.

City of Norman — Council Wards, in the city's ArcGIS Online organization, which says it was "Updated September 13, 2022 by O-2223-8": 8 wards, read 2026-10-16. Its credit line names the City of Norman GIS Services Division, and it states no licence.

City of Lawton — Council Ward, in the city's ArcGIS Online organization, whose service says "Updated-05/12/2023" and whose data was last edited 2 July 2026: 8 wards in 11 records, read 2026-10-21, the ward number alone requested. It does not divide the 2020 census population evenly; it is drawn because the City Clerk's office, asked which map is in force, answered on 2026-10-21 by pointing to the city's public ward map, which draws this layer. It states no licence.

City of Moore — City Wards, layer 20 of its Government_Services service: 3 wards, read 2026-10-16, the ward name alone requested. Its service's credit line names the City of Moore, and it states no licence.
City of Midwest City — Council Wards, layer 0 of its CouncilWards service: 6 wards, read 2026-10-16, the ward number alone requested. It states no licence.
City of Enid — City Wards, in the city's ArcGIS Online organization, last edited 4 August 2025: 6 wards in 7 records, read 2026-10-16. It states no licence.
City of Bartlesville — Wards area, layer 32 of its CityMaps_BvilleGIS service: 5 wards, read 2026-10-16. It states no licence.

City of Shawnee — CityWards, layer 0 of its City_Wards service, last edited 22 September 2026: 6 wards, read 2026-10-16, the ward number alone requested (it is in a field named STATEFP10). It states no licence.

City of Bixby — Council Wards by Color, in the city's ArcGIS Online organization, last edited 26 August 2026, whose population for three of its five wards is exactly the 2020 census count of the ground each covers: 5 wards in 11 records, read 2026-10-16, the ward number alone requested. It states no licence.

source.people: The member or members for each ward, from the same city council roster the City or Town card reads (ok/data/app/ok-city-councils.json), written down from each city's own pages and proved against them by ok/scripts/build_ok_city_councils.py. Which seats a ward elects was read from each city's charter, its own pages, a county election board's results or news reports. Its check holds every drawn ward to a seat its voters elect and every such seat to a drawn ward. Bartlesville's and Bixby's councils choose the mayor from among their members, and the card names the mayor as the member for the ward that elected them.
source.applies: The 10 Oklahoma cities above 25,000 people whose wards elect their own members and are drawn: Bartlesville, Bixby, Enid, Lawton, Midwest City, Moore, Norman, Oklahoma City, Shawnee and Tulsa. Muskogee's wards elect their own members and are not drawn yet; Broken Arrow, Owasso, Jenks and Edmond tie seats to wards and elect every seat by the whole city, and Stillwater's council has no wards. Ground inside a city's Census outline that its map leaves out lies in no ward here.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-09: 634 points in Oklahoma's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Oklahoma — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

layers.label: Tribal Government
layers.rank_note: Tribal areas — Oklahoma has 31, MEASURED by scripts/build_tribal_areas.py: the Osage Reservation, the Shawnee Tribe's 0.430 km² of trust land, 25 Oklahoma Tribal Statistical Areas and 4 joint-use areas; median 523.7 km², between a House district and a unified school district. The statistical areas are drawn by Adam's exception for Oklahoma (2026-10-10), labelled on every card as areas the Census draws to count people.

source.answers: Whether this address is in a tribal area the Census draws, and which nation's government (or nations' governments) it names — 31 areas across 33 nations, most of them Oklahoma Tribal Statistical Areas, which the card says are drawn to count people and are not legal boundaries.

boundary.label: US Census Bureau TIGERweb AIANNHA, current vintage — the Osage Reservation, off-reservation trust land, Oklahoma Tribal Statistical Areas and their joint-use areas, simplified and shipped with the app

source.people: Nobody yet: no Oklahoma nation's council list has been read, and the card says so. The government, its seat and its website come from the Bureau of Indian Affairs' tribal leaders directory (data/bia-tribal-governments.json); the land is joined to the government by this project's own data/tribal-government-join.json.
source.applies: Most of Oklahoma. The Census draws a tribal area over most of the state; the western Panhandle and parts of the north and west lie outside every one.

layers.label: Census County Division
layers.rank_note: 305 census county divisions, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive — median 478.6 km2 of land (mean 582.5), measured 2026-10-15: smaller than the median tribal area, larger on average than a unified school district (400.5 km2 mean)

source.answers: The census county division containing the point, and its county.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 1 (county subdivisions), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 305 features for Oklahoma, every one a census county division (LSADC 22, FUNCSTAT S), measured 2026-10-15.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER. A census county division is an area the Census Bureau draws to report its counts: no one is elected from it, and Oklahoma has no township governments, so the county governs everyone outside a city or town. The card names the division and its county and says it governs nobody.

layers.label: County Commissioner District
layers.rank_note: 231 districts, three in each of the 77 counties; median 715.8 km² (mean 785, from 33.5 to 3,704.5), measured 2026-10-11 — smaller than a House district and larger than the median tribal area

source.answers: Which of the county's three commissioner districts covers the point, and the commissioner the State Election Board lists for it.

boundary.label: Oklahoma Department of Transportation — County Commissioner Districts (ArcGIS FeatureServer layer 0), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 231 features, measured 2026-10-11. Compared on every build with a University of Oklahoma copy, which agrees on 229 of 231 and draws Beaver County's line between Districts 1 and 2 differently; the card says so there. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 20 m interval and refused over a 25 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ok-county-commissioners.json, from the Oklahoma State Election Board's Roster of State and County Officers (the 2024 edition: 229 named, 2 listed vacant), rebuilt weekly by CI, which picks up a newer edition the week it is posted. Home towns printed in the roster are not carried.
source.applies: Oklahoma — statewide, all 231 districts in 77 counties.

anchor_point.note: the State Capitol, Oklahoma City, Oklahoma County

negative_point.note: near Gainesville, Cooke County, TEXAS, about 15 km south of the Red River — outside Oklahoma and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate (minLat 33.50) so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-09: TIGERweb's state layer names Texas at this point (control: the Capitol anchor returns Oklahoma). TEXAS BECAUSE NO INSTANCE SERVES IT, and on land rather than on the Red River, whose channel the county fabric could place on either side.

geometry.note: The whole-Oklahoma outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the 77-county fabric.
The 77 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 5 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120).

Oklahoma's tribal areas (scripts/build_tribal_areas.py) — the Osage Reservation, the Shawnee Tribe's trust land, 25 Oklahoma Tribal Statistical Areas and 4 joint-use areas, simplified by Douglas-Peucker at 20 m and held to a 25 m ceiling. The floor and the ceiling are equal because that is what the Census publishes inside the state on the current vintage, measured 2026-10-10; a change in either direction is a change in the Census's own map and wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The 231 county commissioner districts, three per county (ok/scripts/build_ok_commissioner_districts.py, from the state Department of Transportation). The floor and the ceiling are equal because 19 O.S. 321 fixes three per county.

The 26 judicial districts, dissolved from the county fabric by ok/scripts/build_ok_judicial_districts.py, each carrying its 75 district judge offices' electorates from the State Election Board's 2024 roster.

Oklahoma's 84 conservation districts, pre-built by ok/scripts/build_ok_conservation_districts.py through scripts/published_district_layers.py from the Conservation Commission's map (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m; 106 records joined into 84 shapes; a 33,600-point agreement gate, one group per district, and a coverage check against the county file, both measured 2026-10-16). 635 KB, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on. The floor and the ceiling are equal because the map and the Commission's directory both count 84.

The 64 council wards and districts of the 10 cities above 25,000 people whose wards elect their own members and are drawn, pre-built by ok/scripts/build_ok_city_wards.py through scripts/city_ward_maps.py from the map each city publishes (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m; a 4,000-point agreement gate over the ten cities' extents, measured 100.00%, with no overlap; each map held to its city's Census outline). 138 KB, 33 KB gzipped (measured 2026-10-21), fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

rosters.note: U.S. House (OK) roster, refreshed weekly by update-ok-congress-roster.yml.
Oklahoma Senate roster from Open States, refreshed weekly. The floor is below 48 because a vacant seat is a real event; the export carried 47 on 2026-10-09.
Oklahoma House roster from Open States, refreshed weekly. The floor is below 101 for the same reason; the export carried 100 on 2026-10-09.
One record per commissioner seat from the State Election Board's officer roster, refreshed weekly by update-ok-commissioner-roster.yml. Every seat has a record; a vacant seat carries vacant: true.

Each conservation district's office, telephone and e-mail from the Conservation Commission's directory of district offices, keyed by the district's number on the map, built by ok/scripts/build_ok_conservation_offices.py: 84 offices, no people. The directory is a web page the Commission edits by hand, so this is rebuilt by hand when it changes (ok/WATCH.md).

The five directors of each conservation district that names its board on a website of its own, keyed by the district's number on the map, built by ok/scripts/build_ok_conservation_directors.py: 4 districts and 20 directors, read 2026-10-26. The Commission publishes no list of directors, so the other 80 districts name nobody. Rebuilt by hand quarterly (ok/WATCH.md).

The mayor and council of each of the 16 cities above 25,000 people, keyed by Census place id, written down from each city's own pages (Muskogee's from its election results and news reports) and proved against them by ok/scripts/build_ok_city_councils.py, whose --check holds the file to its seats file, its record of every page read and the drawn wards. Every page it cites is re-read weekly (watch-city-council-pages.yml, listed in the North Carolina worksheet because one root workflow belongs to one instance), which opens a tracking issue when a name or a contact has gone from its page and never edits the file; the seats file is changed by hand (ok/WATCH.md).
The recorded gaps this instance ships with, rendered by the data-gaps panel.
